name: provider-verified annotated tag as immutable release anchor

release_metadata.note: Release metadata itself is not used as immutable authenticity evidence.

origin_rule.name: PROVIDER_VERIFIED_ANNOTATED_TAG_FILE
accept_only_if: tag ref resolves to an annotated tag object rather than only a lightweight tag target
annotated tag object is frozen by exact tag-object SHA
provider reports tag verification.verified=true and reason=valid
tag object target type/commit SHA are explicit
file identity is resolved at that exact target commit SHA
optionally target commit provider verification may be recorded separately but is not needed to infer what object the signed tag names
reject_if: tag is lightweight when a signed-tag premise is required
only release name/page or mutable tag ref name is retained without exact tag-object SHA
file is fetched at a mutable branch rather than exact signed target
origin_rule.semantic_scope: Provider-asserted authenticity of the annotated tag object and its exact target identity, plus repository resolution of a file at that target. It does not make release-page metadata immutable and does not independently verify raw signature cryptography.

comparisons.strength: weak for immutable premise in this live example
comparisons.reason: release immutable=false and release metadata is mutable; use only to discover tag name
exact commit SHA + provider verified=true + exact-ref file identity
exact signed tag object authenticates a named target commit; useful when release intent/name is part of the evidence chain

result.useful_outcome: Scheduled Chat can bind an already-signed public release tag to an exact target commit and exact file identity using only repository verification metadata. This adds release-intent/name anchoring without local cryptographic execution.
result.hosted_compute_boundary: No signing or verification job launched. Existing GitHub provider verification metadata was read; trust remains explicitly provider-based.

frontier: Test a lightweight tag as a negative classification and preserve commit verification as possible fallback but never call it a signed-tag anchor.
Define precedence/choice between signed tag and signed commit origins: tag for release-intent binding, commit for source-state binding; require exact object identities for both.
Use bounded readable-text semantics only after authenticity/identity admission, keeping semantic proof separate from signature verification.
